precepts.text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, men's hearts are set to do evil.
precepts.point: They married the nations' daughters, and the holy seed was mingled.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
The people of Israel, the priests and the Levites “have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing according to their abominations”. They married the nations' daughters, and the holy seed was mixed. It is like that today: the pollution of the Gentiles is evil-ass Christmas. And it is the brothers with an affinity for the white woman, the Japanese, the Moabitess, the Arab; the brothers secretly dealing with prostitutes and escorts; the brothers wasting the holy seed that could have been a prophet, an avenger, your son, and shooting him in a sock and down the drain. You either kill the old man within you, or you are going to catch an STD and be killed. That is the judgment of the Lord.

Why do men keep rolling the dice? Solomon says it: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” The judgment of the Lord for the evil you do in the dark, outside of this congregation, is not executed immediately on brothers and sisters, so the heart, which is the mind, is fully set to keep doing it over and over again.

But things lie dormant. The Lord may let it manifest, bubble and marinate in you, and then say: this brother or sister gives not a damn about my laws; I showed him mercy and longsuffering; now I have to execute him. A slow death: AIDS, HIV, gonorrhea, syphilis. The Lord says, I'm going to get you one way or the next; I gave you a chance to repent, but you are hardheaded. And a hard head makes a soft ass. Then you are crying out to God, and he is not hearing you.

So the delay of the sentence is not permission; it is time to repent. Kill that old man before you are killed.

precepts.text: The commandment was to make no marriages with the nations, not giving daughters to their sons nor taking their daughters, because they would turn the children away from following the Most High.
precepts.point: The sin is interracial marriage with the nations, taking their daughters for themselves and their sons, so that the holy seed mingled itself with the people of those lands. It was not only the common people but the Levites, the leaders, that were chief in this trespass.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
The princes told Ezra that Israel, the priests and the Levites “have not separated themselves from the people of the lands”, taking “of their daughters for themselves, and for their sons: so that the holy seed have mingled themselves with the people of those lands.” The sin is interracial marriage with the nations, the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians and Amorites, and the princes and rulers were chief in it.

The commandment they broke is in Deuteronomy: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” The reason is given too: “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.”

That is why it is a trespass and not a small matter. Marrying the nations turns the children away from following the Most High to serve other gods, and it kindles his anger to destroy suddenly. It was not only the common people but the Levites and the leaders who had done it.

precepts.text: After all our evil deeds and great trespass, the Most High punished us less than our iniquity deserved and gave us such deliverance as this; we deserve far worse, but because of his loving kindness he punished us less.
precepts.point: We cannot take anything we do for granted or get high-minded in this truth and think we cannot be touched. Remember this one thing above all.

note.label: Psalm 36: The Transgression of the Wicked

precepts.why:
“Thy mercy, O Lord, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds. Thy righteousness is like the great mountains; thy judgments are a great deep”. Ezra shows what that mercy looks like on Israel: “after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this”. We deserve far worse, but because of his lovingkindness he punished us less than our iniquity deserved and gave us such deliverance as this.

That is why we cannot take anything we do for granted, or get high-minded in this truth and think we cannot be touched. What we have is mercy. Remember this one thing above all.

precepts.text: Ezra says the Most High punished us less than our iniquities deserve, agreeing with David.
precepts.point: As far as the east is from the west, so far He removes our transgressions; He pities them that fear Him, for He knows we are dust.

note.label: Psalm 103: Bless the Lord for His Benefits to Israel

precepts.why:
“He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.” Ezra says the same in his prayer: “And after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this”.

The Most High punished us less than our iniquities deserve. Ezra the prophet agrees with David the prophet, and to this agree the words of the prophets. Israel's evil deeds and great trespass brought what came upon us, and still it was less than we deserved, and he gave deliverance.

That mercy and grace is to Israel, and it is not so that we could continue in sin. Christ came to forgive Israel of their sins, and this is the mercy David and Ezra both bless him for.

precepts.text: One of His benefits is that the Most High has punished us less than our iniquities deserve and has given us such deliverance.
precepts.point: What shall I render unto the Lord for all His benefits toward me? The apostle Paul answered that question.

note.label: Psalm 116: I Love the Lord Because He Hath Heard My Voice

precepts.why:
One of his benefits is this: “after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this”.

The Most High has punished us less than our iniquities deserve and has given us such deliverance. When the psalm asks what shall I render unto the Lord for all his benefits, that is counted among them: he preserved the simple, we were brought low and he helped us, and he did not give us all that our evil deeds deserved.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

points: Give not your daughters unto their sons, neither take their daughters unto your sons: that's the law. Nor seek their peace or their wealth for ever, that ye may be strong: that's how you're strong, by staying within your own nation. When you stick with your own people, you strengthen your race; when you go and sleep with another nation, you weaken yourself and your race.

note.label: Are You A Strong Independent Woman?

points: Should we again break thy commandments, and join in affinity with the people of these abominations? When you abandon your nation, that's an abomination. Wouldest not thou be angry with us till thou hadst consumed us? God will create bad conditions for you and judgment will come your way.

points: When Ezra hears this thing he rends his garment and his mantle, plucks off the hair of his head and beard, and sits down astonished, in distress that the people did this after the Most High showed mercy to bring them out of Babylon.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: Then everyone that trembled at the words of the God of Israel assembles to him because of the transgression of those that had been carried away, and he sits astonished until the evening sacrifice.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: At the evening sacrifice Ezra rises from his heaviness, and having rent his garment and mantle, falls upon his knees and spreads out his hands unto the Lord his God.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: He says he is ashamed and blushes to lift up his face, for their iniquities are increased over their head and their trespass is grown up unto the heavens. Since the days of the fathers they have been in a great trespass unto this day.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: For their iniquities they, their kings, and their priests have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, and to spoil. The nation is privy to all the captivities it came from, Egypt, Assyria, and Babylon, and knows why it went, yet does the same sins.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: Now for a little space grace has been showed from the Lord to leave a remnant to escape and to give them a nail in his holy place, that the Most High may lighten their eyes and give a little reviving in their bondage.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: Though they were bondmen the Most High has not forsaken them but extended mercy in the sight of the kings of Persia, to give a reviving to set up the house of God and give them a wall in Jerusalem. This is the very leeway that let them come back to the land.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: Ezra asks what they shall say after this, for they have forsaken the commandments. It is like a parent giving you something good and you turning and doing something to make him feel wrong for giving it.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: The commandment given by the prophets said the land they go to possess is an unclean land, filled from one end to another with the filthiness and abominations of the people of the lands.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: Therefore they were not to give their sons or take their daughters, nor seek their peace or wealth, that they might be strong, eat the good of the land, and leave it for an inheritance to their children forever. This command is reiterated all the way back to the time of Moses.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: After all that has come upon them for their evil deeds, and seeing the Most High has punished their iniquities less than they deserve and given such deliverance, Ezra asks should they again break the commandments and join in affinity with the people of these abominations.

note.label: Ezra 9: Ezra Mourns the Strange Wives

points: Would not the Most High be angry until he had consumed them so there should be no remnant left. Oh Lord God of Israel, thou art righteous, for they remain yet escaped as it is this day.

They stand before the Most High in their trespass, for they cannot stand before him because of it. Even though the Levites and Israel committed this sin, the Most High still showed them mercy and let them stay in the land.
